messages.subject: longitudinal Rasch model
parts:
Hi phil

I'm trying to perform a confirmatory analysis using Rasch model. my procedure is as follows: I estimate rasch model at each time point separately and check for fit indices, then I estimate a series of nested constrained model longitudinaly (configural, metric and scalar)

My question is: is it necessary to check for metric invariance (equality of factor loadings) since in the Rasch model they are already set equal?

Thank you in advance for your precious support.

Lina.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: longitudinal Rasch model
parts:
Hi Lina,

What you are describing sounds more like a multiple-group type question than a longitudinal model. For latent longitudinal models to work you generally have to have a stronger type of invariance assumed in order to properly equate the time points (e.g., the intercept in the first item wave 1 must be equal to the first intercept wave 2 and 3, so that changes can be expressed in terms of population mean differences; same type of reasoning for latent growth curves). Rasch models are a bit easier because the slopes are already constrained to be equal by default, so this makes them rather appealing if they turn out to be suitable for the data. HTH.

Phil
